what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 3: The normalization of the equal-level kernel in the ordered 3+1 formation law. Executed (first look): in the ordered sphere formation law on three-dimensional level planes the low-k structure factor is 0.96-0.97 of the linear kernel sigma^2/(1 - |phi|^2) at beta = 2 and 6; in 2+1 block 35 (PR #8180) found 0.83-0.97 rising with beta. TASK: derive the leading correction: S(k) (1 - |phi(k)|^2)/sigma^2 = 1 - a/beta + O(1/beta^2) as k -> 0, with a explicit (expected to involve the plateau |m|^2 and the return sum G_3 = (2 pi)^-3 Int 1/(1 - |phi|^2)); route: expand the one-step map of the transverse field to third order in the fluctuations (the record is a von Mises-Fisher draw about S/|S| with concentration beta |S|), close the hierarchy at Gaussian order, and compare with the simulator's shells (probes/lib/formation_levelplane.py) at beta = 3, 6, 12, 24. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/kernel-normalization-in-3plus1/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/kernel-normalization-in-3plus1/<name>/check.py"
